task.title: Say why the board moved when the default port falls back
task.description:
Deferred from PR #25 (WB-01KZC3D44DWD9G99SX7D3PVJ3H, feat/serve-port-fallback) as a minor review finding.

internal/cli/run.go:827-846 implements the fallback and :913 prints the banner. The banner prints only the resolved address ("Workbook board: http://127.0.0.1:53321"); it never says the default 127.0.0.1:7331 was taken, so the collision is silent.

Why it matters: before this change a second bind died loudly with 'open board listener: ... address already in use', which was a strong signal that something was squatting the port. Now a squatted default is indistinguishable from the intended two-projects-on-one-machine case. In the threat model this project already states (a compromised agent or malicious dependency), a squatter can bind 127.0.0.1:7331, serve a look-alike board, and harvest task titles/descriptions from a user who opens their habitual bookmark while the real board hides on an OS-assigned port.

Amplifier (pre-existing, NOT introduced by PR #25): the real board's mutating API in internal/webui/handler.go has no Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site/CSRF check, so an impostor page can also scan for and drive the real board through the user's browser. Worth tracking separately if this ticket does not cover it.

Proposed fix: when the fallback fires, print why -- e.g. '127.0.0.1:7331 is in use; serving on http://127.0.0.1:53321 instead' -- so a squatted default is visible rather than silent. Roughly a one-line change plus a test; openBoardListenerWith already knows the fallback happened and would need to signal it to runServe (return a flag, or have runServe compare listener.Addr() against the requested addr).

Deferred rather than fixed in PR #25 because the accepted ticket scope explicitly chose 'the banner already prints listener.Addr(), no other change', and the reviewer rated it non-blocking.
